rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before the request, Benjamin says Joseph's brothers had mistreated Joseph and stolen him; when asked who put the cup in his baggage, he blames the same person who put the dirhams in theirs, and they rebuke him for mentioning the money lest they be seized.
rows.anchor: ما لقينا من ابني راحيل يوسف وأخيه؟ فقال بنيامين: ما لقي ابنا راحيل منك؟ أما يوسف، فقد فعلتم به ما فعلتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers call Joseph al-Aziz because Egypt had come under him and he was the king's treasurer.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن أرض مصر صارت إليه، وهو خازن الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their father is Benjamin's father, an old man grieving a lost son; they ask Joseph to take one of them in Benjamin's place, appealing to his beneficence toward them.
rows.anchor: حزينا على ابن مفقود، { فخذ أحدنا مكانه إنا نراك من المحسنين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ma'adh Allah means seeking God's protection; taking the person found with their property means detaining him for theft.
rows.anchor: يقول: نعوذ بالله { أن نأخذ } ، يعني أن نحبس بالسرقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph says taking an innocent person in place of the guilty one would make them unjust.
rows.anchor: أن نأخذ البرىء مكان السقيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers give up hope of recovering Benjamin and withdraw to confer privately.
rows.anchor: { فلما استيأسوا منه } ، يقول: يئسوا من بنيامين، { خلصوا نجيا } ، يعني خلوا يتناجون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their 'greatest' brother is Judah, the one most esteemed and learned among them, not their oldest by age.
rows.anchor: يعني عظيمهم في أنفسهم وأعلمهم، وهو يهوذا، ولم يكن أكبرهم في السن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob had taken a covenant from them to bring Benjamin back; earlier they had neglected Joseph, and Judah will stay in Egypt until his father permits return or God rules in his favor by restoring Benjamin.
rows.anchor: يعني في أمر بنيامين لتأتينه به، { ومن قبل } بنيامين { ما فرطتم في يوسف } ، يعني ضيعتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'Best of judges' means the best adjudicators.
rows.anchor: يعني أفضل القاضين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers tell Jacob Benjamin stole and say they reported only what they knew: they did not foresee his theft and would not have brought him had they known.
rows.anchor: يعني وما كنا نرى أنه يسرق، ولو علمنا ما ذهبنا به معنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The village is Egypt; the brothers ask Jacob to verify the theft with its people and with the caravan they traveled in, insisting they tell the truth.
rows.anchor: يعني مصر، { التي كنا فيها } أنه سرق، { والعير التي أقبلنا فيها وإنا لصادقون } [آية: 82] فيما نقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob observes that each time his sons travel one is lost: Joseph had detained Benjamin and kept Simeon and Judah, so Jacob suspects them.
rows.anchor: قال لهم يعقوب: كلما ذهبتم نقص منكم واحد، وكان يوسف، عليه السلام، حبس بنيامين، وأقام شمعون ويهوذا، فاتهمهم يعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob says their souls have made the affair seem good to them; beautiful patience is patience without anxious complaint, and he hopes God will return all four sons.
rows.anchor: يعني ولكن زينت لكم { أنفسكم أمرا } ، كان هو منكم هذا، { فصبر جميل } ، يعني صبرا حسنا لا جزع فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is all-knowing of His creatures and wise, meaning judge over them; God withheld Joseph's story from Jacob to test his patience.
rows.anchor: بخلقه، { الحكيم } [آية: 83]، يعني الحاكم فيهم، ولم يخبر الله يعقوب بأمر يوسف ليختبر صبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob turns away from his sons toward himself and cries, 'Alas, my sorrow for Joseph'; his eyes were white and sightless for six years from grief, while sorrow churned within him.
rows.anchor: يعني وأعرض يعقوب عن بنيه، ثم أقبل على نفسه، { وقال يأسفا } ، يعني يا حزناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob's sons reproach him: by God, he will keep remembering Joseph until he is debilitated or dead.
rows.anchor: أي قال بنوه يعيرونه: { تالله تفتأ } ، يعني والله ما تزال { تذكر يوسف حتى تكون حرضا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob's 'bathi' is grief he has spread among people, while his 'huzn' is inward grief; he directs both complaints to God.
rows.anchor: يعني ما بثه في الناس، { وحزني } ، يعني ما بطن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What Jacob knows from God is the certain fulfillment of Joseph's dream.
rows.anchor: يعني من تحقيق رؤيا يوسف أنه كائن { ما لا تعلمون } [آية: 86]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob tells his sons to search for Joseph and Benjamin; 'God's rawh' means God's mercy, and only unbelievers despair of it.
rows.anchor: يعني فابحثوا عن { يوسف وأخيه } بنيامين، { ولا تيأسوا من روح الله } ، يعني من رحمة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob dreamed that the Angel of Death said he had not taken Joseph's soul and gave Jacob good news; on waking, Jacob ordered the search.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن يعقوب، عليه السلام، رأى ملك الموت في المنام، فقال له: هل قبضت روح يوسف؟ قال: لا، وبشره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob's grandsons swear he remains in his old 'misguidance,' meaning hardship and distress from loving and remembering Joseph; forty years had not made him forget.
rows.anchor: يقول: في شقاء وعناء، يعني في شقاء من حب يوسف وذكره، فما تنساه وقد أتى عليه أربعون سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording is illustrated by the cited expression in al-Qamar 54:24.
rows.anchor:
إني إذا لفي ضلال مبين
[القمر: 24]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bearer of good news was the person who had earlier taken the first shirt stained with blood; he laid the shirt on Jacob's face, restoring his sight after the whiteness.
rows.anchor: فلما أتاه البشير، وهو الذي ذهب بالقميص الأول الذى كان عليه الدم، { وألقى القميص على وجه يعقوب، { فارتد }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob's reminder that he knows what others do not know refers to the certain fulfillment of Joseph's dream, as he had said in 12:86.
rows.anchor:
إنمآ أشكو بثي وحزني إلى الله وأعلم من الله ما لا تعلمون
[يوسف: 86]، من تحقيق رؤيا يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sons ask Jacob to seek forgiveness for their wrongdoing concerning Joseph.
rows.anchor: استغفر لنا ذنوبنآ إنا كنا خاطئين } [آية: 97] في أمر يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob says he will seek his Lord's forgiveness for them during the late night before dawn; God forgives sins and shows mercy to believers.
rows.anchor: سحرا من الليل، { إنه هو الغفور } للذنوب، { الرحيم } [آية: 98] بالمؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob and his household enter Egypt and Joseph gathers them to himself, inviting them to enter safely from fear; the arriving party numbered seventy-two men and women.
rows.anchor: يعني يعقوب وأهله أرض مصر، { على يوسف آوى } ، يعني ضم { إليه أبويه وقال } لهم: { ادخلوا مصر إن شآء الله آمنين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph seats his parents on the throne-bed, one at his right and one at his left; Rachel had died, so the woman was Jacob's aunt, whom Joseph raised there.
rows.anchor: يعني على السرير، وجعل أحدهما عن يمينه، والآخر عن يساره، وكانت أمه راحيل قد ماتت، وخالته تحت يعقوب

rows.speaker: أبو صالح
rows.claim: The prostration of Jacob, his aunt, and his brothers occurred before Joseph raised them onto the bed; Abu Salih calls it a greeting prostration, not worship.
rows.anchor: قال أبو صالح: هذه سجدة التحية، لا سجدة العبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph calls the prostration the realization of his earlier dream; forty years passed between the dream and its fulfillment.
rows.anchor: يعني تحقيق { رؤياي من قبل قد جعلها ربي حقا } ، يعني صدقا، وكان بين رؤيا يوسف وبين تصديقها أربعون سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God did good by freeing Joseph from prison and bringing his family from their nomadic life of tents and livestock after Satan caused division between him and his brothers.
rows.anchor: وجآء بكم من البدو } ، كانوا أهل عمود مواشى، { من بعد أن نزغ } ، يعني أزاغ { الشيطان بيني وبين إخوتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is subtle in accomplishing what He wills: He freed Joseph from prison and the well, reunited the family, and removed Satan's incitement against the brothers from Joseph's heart.
rows.anchor: حين أخرجه من السجن ومن البئر، وجمع بينه وبين أهل بيته بعد التفريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob died two years before Joseph; Jacob and Esau, Isaac's sons born from one womb at the same hour, shared a grave.
rows.anchor: مات يعقوب قبل يوسف بسنتين، ودفن يعقوب والعيص بن إسحاق في قبر واحد، وخرجا من بطن واحد، في ساعة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After God reunited Joseph's family and granted him royal ease, Joseph longed for God and His signs and wished for death.
rows.anchor: فلما جمع الله ليوسف شمله، فأقر بعينه، وهو مغموس في الملك والنعمة، اشتاق إلى الله وإلى آياته، فتمنى الموت

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that no prophet ever wished for death except Joseph.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: لم يتمن الموت نبى قط غير يوسف، عليه السلام، قال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph received rule over Egypt for eighty years and was taught interpretation of dreams; the preposition in 'from the interpretation' is extra.
rows.anchor: على أهل مصر ثمانين سنة، { وعلمتني من تأويل الأحاديث } ، من هاهنا صلة، يعني تعبير الرؤيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'Originator of the heavens and earth' means their Creator; Joseph asks God as his protector in both lives to take him sincerely devoted to His oneness and join him to his father Jacob, Isaac, and Abraham.
rows.anchor: يعني خالق السموات والأرض، كن { أنت وليي في الدنيا والآخرة توفني مسلما } ، يعني مخلصا بتوحيدك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is unseen news: Joseph, Jacob, and his sons had been hidden from Muhammad until God revealed the account to him; Muhammad had not witnessed or known it.
rows.anchor: غاب يا محمد أمر يوسف ويعقوب وبنيه عنك حتى أعلمناك، { نوحيه إليك } ، لم تشهدوه ولم تعلمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet was not with Joseph's brothers when they agreed on their plan and plotted against him.
rows.anchor: يعني عند إخوة يوسف، { إذ أجمعوا أمرهم وهم يمكرون } [آية: 102] بيوسف، عليه السلام.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'Most people' means the unbelievers of Mecca, who will not believe even if Muhammad is eager for them to do so; the clause has fronting.
rows.anchor: يعني كفار مكة، { ولو حرصت بمؤمنين } [آية: 103]، يعني بمصدقين، فيها تقديم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet asks no payment for their faith; the Quran is only a reminder for all peoples.
rows.anchor: يعني على الإيمان من جعل، { إن هو } ، يعني القرآن، { إلا ذكر للعالمين } [آية: 104]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Heavenly signs include sun, moon, stars, clouds, winds, and rain; earthly signs include mountains, seas, trees, and plants recurring year after year.
rows.anchor: الشمس، والقمر، والنجوم، والسحاب، والرياح، والمطر، { والأرض } الجبال، والبحور، والشجر، والنبات، عاما بعد عام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People pass by the signs by seeing them yet turning away; they should reflect on God's works and affirm His oneness.
rows.anchor: يعني يرونها، { وهم عنها معرضون } [آية: 105]، أفلا يتفكرون فيما يرون من صنع الله فيوحدونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most people of Mecca affirm God created them and all things, yet remain polytheists because they worship idols.
rows.anchor: أي أكثر أهل مكة، { بالله إلا وهم مشركون } [آية: 106] في إيمانهم، فإذا سئلوا: من خلقهم وخلق الأشياء كلها؟ قالوا: الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A 'covering' is worldly punishment that envelops them; the Hour may also come suddenly while they are unaware, making this a threat.
rows.anchor: يعني أن تغشاهم عقوبة، { من عذاب الله } في الدنيا، { أو تأتيهم الساعة بغتة } ، يعني فجأة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The path is the religion of Islam and the Prophet's practice; calling to God means calling people to know God through monotheism, with clear proof.
rows.anchor: ملة الإسلام، { سبيلي } ، يعني سنتي، { أدعو إلى الله } ، يعني إلى معرفة الله، وهو التوحيد، { على بصيرة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet and those who follow his religion call to this path.
rows.anchor: يعني على بيان، { أنا ومن اتبعني } على ديني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God declares Himself above the partners ascribed to Him, and the Prophet disavows associationism.
rows.anchor: نزه الرب نفسه عن شركهم، { ومآ أنا من المشركين } [آية: 108].

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier messengers were men from settled towns because their people were more rational and knowledgeable than nomadic tent-dwellers; this answers Meccan unbelievers who demanded an angel messenger.
rows.anchor: لأن أهل الريف أعقل وأعلم من أهل العمود، وذلك حين قال كفار مكة بألا بعث الله ملكا رسولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The destroyed predecessors include Aad, Thamud, and earlier nations; the Hereafter is better than worldly life for those who avoid associationism.
rows.anchor: يعنى من قبل أهل مكة، كان عاقبتهم الهلاك في الدنيا، يعنى قوم عاد، وثمود، والأمم الخالية، { ولدار الآخرة خير }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Messengers despair of their people's belief and warn of promised worldly punishment; the people think the warning has been false, then divine aid comes and the messengers and chosen believers are rescued, while no one can repel God's punishment from criminals.
rows.anchor: من إيمان قومهم،أوعدتهم رسلهم العذاب في الدنيا بأنه نازل بهم، { وظنوا أنهم قد كذبوا } حسب قوم الرسل قد كذبوهم العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran's accounts teach the victory of messengers and destruction of their peoples, as recounted in Ta-Sin Mim, al-Qamar, Hud, and al-Araf; they instruct people of understanding.
rows.anchor: يعني في خبرهم، يعني نصر الرسل، وهلاك قومهم حين خبر الله عنهم في كتابه في طسم الشعراء، وفى اقتربت الساعة،وفى سورة هود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran is not fabricated, contrary to Meccan unbelievers' claim that Muhammad made it up; it confirms that the earlier scriptures are all from God.
rows.anchor: هذا القرآن { حديثا يفترى } يعني يتقول لقول كفار مكة: إن محمدا تقوله من تلقاء نفسه، { ولكن تصديق } الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran clarifies everything, guides away from error, and brings protection from punishment to those who believe it is from God.
rows.anchor: يقول: فيه بيان { كل شيء و } هو { وهدى } من الضلالة، { ورحمة } من العذاب، { لقوم يؤمنون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'Glory' here means wondrous; the night journey took the Prophet in Rajab from the Sacred Mosque to Jerusalem, one year before the Hijra.
rows.anchor: { سبحان } ، يعني عجب، { الذي أسرى بعبده } ، في رجب، يعني النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، { ليلا من المسجد الحرام إلى المسجد الأقصى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The five daily prayers were prescribed for the Prophet on the night of the journey.
rows.anchor: قبل الهجرة بسنة، وفرضت عليه الصلوات الخمس تلك الليلة، وعرضت على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ثلاثة أنهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Three rivers of milk, honey, and wine were shown to the Prophet; he refused the wine, and Gabriel said God had forbidden it to his community.
rows.anchor: وعرضت على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ثلاثة أنهار: نهر من لبن، ونهر من عسل، ونهر من خمر، فلم يشرب النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blessing around the Farthest Mosque consists of water, trees, and goodness.
rows.anchor: يعني بالبركة الماء، والشجر، والخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Among the signs shown to the Prophet were the Buraq, men, and angels, and he prayed with the prophets.
rows.anchor: فكان مما رأى من الآيات البراق، والرجال، والملائكة، وصلى بالنبيين تلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet tells Umm Hani that he prayed Isha and Fajr in Mecca, with the prayer between them in Jerusalem.
rows.anchor: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أصبح بمكة ليلة أسري به من مكة، فقال لأم هانئ ابنة أبي طالب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel took the Prophet's hand as he lay down before sleep; Michael waited at the door with a mount taller than a donkey and shorter than a mule, with humanlike face, horse features, two wings, cowlike tail and hooves, and a stride reaching his sight.
rows.anchor: وقد أخذت مضجعي من الفراش قبل أن أنام، وأخذ بيدي وأخرجني من الباب وميكائيل، عليه السلام، بالباب ومعه دابة، فوق الحمار ودون البغل، ووجهها كوجه الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mount was mottled and oddly formed; Solomon used it to travel a month's distance in one morning, and the angels carried the Prophet swiftly to Jerusalem.
rows.anchor: سيلاء، مضطربة الخلق، لها جناحان، ذنبها كذنب البقر، وحافرها كأظلاف البقر، خطوها عند منتهى بصرها، كان سليمان بن داود، عليه السلام، يغدو عليها مسيرة شهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At Jerusalem, the prophets were presented to the Prophet, who led them in prayer and saw many wonders.
rows.anchor: ثم أخذ يزفان بي حتى أتيت بيت المقدس، ومثل لي النبيون، فصليت بهم، ورأيت ورأيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Umm Hani grabs the Prophet's garment and warns that disbelievers will mock him and believers may doubt if he tells Quraysh; he insists on going even if they deny him.
rows.anchor: فوالله ليجترأن عليك المكذب، وليمترين فيك المصدق، قال: " وإن كذبوني لأخرجن "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet goes to Quraysh elders seated in the Hijr, calls the journey a marvel, and repeats that he prayed Isha and Fajr in Mecca and between them at Jerusalem, leading and speaking with prophets.
rows.anchor: فخرج إلى المسجد، فإذا فيه شيوخ من شيوخ قريش جلوس في الحجر، فقام عليهم فقال: " ألا أحدثكم بالعجب؟ "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers accept the Prophet's account of the night journey, while polytheists reject it.
rows.anchor: فصدقه المؤمنون، وكذبه المشركون.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mut'im ibn Adi calls the Prophet a liar and sorcerer, saying Jerusalem takes forty days to reach even with great hardship, and regrets not having seized him.
rows.anchor: ما ثكلتني يدي على هذا الكذاب ألا لن أكون ذلك اليوم جزعا، فآخذك بيدي أخذا، تخبرنا أنك صليت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Quraysh tells Abu Bakr that the Prophet claims to have prayed in Jerusalem between the two Meccan prayers, Abu Bakr says that if he said it, it is true.
rows.anchor: فقالت قريش: يا أبا بكر، ألا تسمع ما يقول صاحبك، يزعم أنه صلى العشاء الآخرة والفجر بمكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Bakr asks for details of Jerusalem's gate, building, pillars, and rock; after the Prophet describes them, Abu Bakr embraces him, affirms him, and is called al-Siddiq that day; his name is Atiq ibn Uthman ibn Amr ibn Kab ibn Murra.
rows.anchor: فأخبره النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، فالتزمه أبو بكر، فقال: أشهد أنك صادق، فسمى يومئذ الصديق، اسمه: عتيق بن عثمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet describes Jesus as white, medium in stature, broad-chested, curly-haired, reddish, and most like Urwa ibn Mutib al-Thaqafi.
rows.anchor:
قال المسلمون: يا رسول الله، كيف رأيت الأنبياء، عليهم السلام؟ قال:
" رأيت عيسى ابن مريم صلى الله عليه وسلم رجلا أبيض، فوق الربعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses is described as tall, very dark, muscular, with abundant straight hair, resembling men of Azd Shanu'a; hair would show through two shirts.
rows.anchor: ورأيت موسى، عليه السلام، رجلا طويلا، آدم شديد الأدمة، ضرب اللحم، سبط الشعر أشعر كأنه من رجال أزد شنوءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham most resembles the Prophet in form and character and greets him first with a handshake and prayer for mercy.
rows.anchor: ورأيت إبراهيم، عليه السلام، أشبه الناس بي خلقا وخلقا، فبدأني بالسلام والمصافحة والترحم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Dajjal is described as large, corpulent, dark, curly-haired, thick-bearded, one-eyed, bright-foreheaded, bright-toothed, with 'kafir' written between his eyes and resembling Futn ibn Abd al-Uzza.
rows.anchor: ورأيت الدجال، رجلا جسيما، لحيما، آدم، جعد الرأس، كث اللحية، ممسوح العين، أحلى الجبهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amr ibn Rabi'a and al-Harith ibn Kab ibn Amr are seen dragging their entrails through the Fire because they first instituted forbidden livestock customs, named and commanded worship of al-Lat and al-Uzza, altered Abraham's monotheistic religion, and set idols around the Kaaba.
rows.anchor: وعليهما وفرة يجران قصبهما في النار " ، يعني أمعاءهما، قيل للنبى صلى الله عليه وسلم: ولم؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amr ibn Rabi'a was short and most resembled Aktham ibn al-Jawn al-Khuza'i; when Aktham asks whether resemblance harms him, the Prophet says no, since Aktham is a believer and Amr an unbeliever.
rows.anchor: فأما عمرو بن ربيعة، فهو رجل قصير، أشبه الناس به هذا، يعني أكثم بن الجون الخزاعى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Qurayshi tells Mut'im he judged his nephew too quickly, then mockingly asks the Prophet about Quraysh's caravans on the road.
rows.anchor: فقال رجل من كفار قريش للمطعم بن عدى: عجلت على ابن أخيك، ثم قال كهيئة المستهزئ: رويدك يا محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet describes a caravan at al-Rawha with a lost camel being sought; he passed its men, drank and made ablution from their vessel, and tells Quraysh to ask them.
rows.anchor: رأيت عير بنى فلان بالروحاء نزولا، قد ضلت لهم ناقة، وهم في طلبها، فمررت على رجالهم وليس بها أحد منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He describes another caravan in a specified valley and night hour: its camels fled, a red camel broke a leg, and its people were splinting it.
rows.anchor: ومررت على عير بني فلان، في وادي كذا وكذا، في ساعة كذا وكذا من الليل، ومعي جبريل وميكائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asked where the caravan was, he says it was near Tan'im before dawn and would arrive immediately; he predicts its loads and people, noting a fallen cloak retrieved by an Abyssinian and placed on the last camel.
rows.anchor: تركتها بالتنعيم قبيل " ، قال: فإن كنت صادقا، فهي قادمة الأن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God displays the caravan to the Prophet, who gives its count, loads, people, and leading gray camel; it arrives from the Tan'im pass as described.
rows.anchor: فبينا هو صلى الله عليه وسلم يحدثهم، إذ مثل الله عز وجل له كل شىء حتى نظر إلى عدتها وأحمالها ومن فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the caravan details prove accurate, the polytheists call the Prophet an obvious sorcerer, and Quraysh refrains from some harm for a year.
rows.anchor: وإذا هي وأحمالها وعدتها وما فيها كما قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، فقال المشركون: لقد صدق الوليد بن المغيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gave Moses the Torah as guidance from error for the Israelites; 'do not take a trustee besides Me' has fronting in its wording.
rows.anchor: يقول: أعطينا موسى التوراة، { وجعلناه هدى } ، يعني التوراة هدى، { لبني إسرائيل } من الضلالة، { ألا تتخذوا من دوني وكيلا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'Descendants of those carried with Noah' addresses Adam's progeny and means their forebears; they too are told not to take a guardian besides God.
rows.anchor: يا { ذرية } آدم، { من حملنا مع نوح } في السفينة، ألا تتخذوا من دوني وكيلا، يعني الأهل، يعني وليا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah is praised as a grateful servant because he remembered God and praised Him while eating, drinking, standing, sitting, dressing, entering, leaving, sleeping, waking, walking, and working.
rows.anchor: فكان من شكره أنه كان يذكر الله عز وجل حين يأكل ويشرب، ويحمد الله تعالى حين يفرغ، ويذكر الله سبحانه حين يقوم ويقعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God covenanted with Israel in the Torah that they would corrupt the land twice, 210 years apart; their great exalting means oppressing others severely through disobedience until humbled.
rows.anchor: يقول: وعهدنا إليهم في التوراة، { لتفسدن } ، لتهلكن { في الأرض مرتين } ، فكان بين الهلاكين مائتا سنة وعشر سنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first destruction came through Bukhtanassar the Magian king of Babylon and his men, who killed people in streets, captured children, ruined Jerusalem, placed corpses there, burned the Torah, and took captives to Babylon for seventy years.
rows.anchor: بختنصر المجوسى ملك بابل وأصحابه، { فجاسوا خلال الديار } ، يعني فقتل الناس في الأزقة، وسبى ذراريهم، وخرب بيت المقدس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cyrus son of Mazdak the Persian rescued Israel and returned them to Jerusalem; God increased their wealth and children, and they remained there 210 years with prophets among them.
rows.anchor: على يد كروس بن مزدك الفارس، فردهم إلى بيت المقدس، فذلك قوله عز وجل: { ثم رددنا لكم الكرة عليهم وأمددناكم بأموال وبنين } ، حتى كثروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After renewed disobedience, Antiochus son of Sisy, Roman ruler of Nineveh, brought the second destruction: he killed and captured Israelites, ruined Jerusalem, killed scholars, and burned the Torah.
rows.anchor: فعادا إلى المعاصي الثانية، فسلط الله عليهم أيضا انطباخوس بن سيس الرومي ملك أرض نينوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second invaders entered Jerusalem as Bukhtanassar had before; 'tabbiran' means to destroy thoroughly, as in al-Furqan 25:39.
rows.anchor: انطياخوس بن سيس ومن معه بيت المقدس، { كما دخلوه أول مرة } ، يقول: كما دخله بختنصر المجوسي وأصحابه قبل ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase in al-Furqan 25:39, 'we destroyed them all,' explains tabbara as destroying; God may show mercy and spare Israel killing and captivity.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God later rescued Israel through al-Miqyas, returned them to Jerusalem, restored their solidarity, and sent prophets among them.
rows.anchor: ثم إن الله عز وجل استنقذهم على يدي المقياس، فردهم إلى بيت المقدس فعمروه، ورد الله عز وجل إليهم ألفتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their return to sin and disbelief brought a worse assault: after they killed Yahya ibn Zakariya, Titus (also called Istafabous) killed 180,000 Jews, captured their children, burned the Torah, ruined Jerusalem, and polluted it with corpses and pigs; it remained ruined until Muslims rebuilt it.
rows.anchor: فعادوا إلى الكفر، وقتلوا يحيى بن زكريا، فسلط الله عيلهم ططس بن استاتوس الرومي، ويقال: اصطفابوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gehenna is a prison from which unbelievers never leave; the wording is compared with 2:273, where the restrained poor are held in God's path.
rows.anchor:
يعني محبسا لا يخرجون منها أبدا، كقوله عز وجل:
للفقرآء الذين أحصروا
[البقرة: 273]، يعني حبسوا في سبيل الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran guides by calling people to what is most upright, the soundest course, and promises believers who affirm it and do good a great reward in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: يعني يدعو، { للتي هي أقوم } ، يعني أصوب، { ويبشر } القرآن، { المؤمنين } ، يعني المصدقين، { الذين يعملون الصالحات } من الأعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who disbelieve in the resurrection and its recompense for deeds face a painful punishment.
rows.anchor: يعني بالبعث الذي فيه جزاء الأعمال، { أعتدنا لهم عذابا أليما } [آية: 10]، يعني عذابا وجيعا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person praying for evil against himself is al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, who demanded punishment in 8:32, just as people pray for good for themselves.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human haste is illustrated by Adam trying to sit when the spirit had reached only his middle, before reaching his feet; al-Nadr similarly hastened his self-directed curse, and humanity inherited haste from Adam.
rows.anchor: يعني آدم، عليه السلام، حين نفخ فيه الروح من قبل رأسه، فلما بلغت الروح وسطه عجل، فأراد أن يجلس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night and day began as two illuminated signs whose brightness made them hard to distinguish; God erased the moon's sign, the dark mark at its center, removing sixty-nine parts out of seventy of the sun's light.
rows.anchor: يعني علامتين مضيئتين، فكان ضوء القمر مثل ضوء الشمس، فلم يعرف الليل من النهار، يقول الله تعالى: { فمحونآ آية الليل }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun remains the visible day sign; daylight lets people seek provision, count years and calculate, and God has explained everything clearly.
rows.anchor: يعني أقررنا ضوءها فيها، { لتبتغوا فضلا من ربكم } ، يعني رزقا، { ولتعلموا } بها { عدد السنين والحساب وكل شيء فصلناه تفصيلا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each person's deed, good or bad, is fastened to the neck and stays with that person until the reckoning; on Resurrection Day the deed-record is opened and handed over.
rows.anchor: يعني عمله الذي عمل، خيرا كان أو شرا، فهو { في عنقه } لا يفارقه حتى يحاسب عليه، { ونخرج له يوم القيامة كتابا يلقاه منشورا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person is told to read the book; 'enough is yourself as reckoner' means a witness better than oneself cannot be found.
rows.anchor:
يعني شهيدا، فلا شاهد عليك أفضل من نفسك، وذلك حين قالوا:
والله ربنا ما كنا مشركين
[الأنعام: 23]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When people claim they were not polytheists in 6:23, God seals their tongues and makes their limbs testify to associationism and denial; this illustrates the verse's self-witnessing.
rows.anchor:
والله ربنا ما كنا مشركين
[الأنعام: 23]، ختم الله على ألسنتهم، ثم أمر الجوارح، فشهدت عليه بشركه وتكذيبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parallel in 75:14 means a person's own limbs testify against them, including the self, tongue, hands, and feet.
rows.anchor:
بل الإنسان على نفسه بصيرة
[القيامة: 14]، يعني جوارحهم حين شهدت عليهم أنفسهم، وألسنتهم، وأيديهم، وأرجلهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance benefits the guided person, while straying from guidance leaves that person's own sin upon them.
rows.anchor: { من اهتدى فإنما يهتدي لنفسه } الخير، { ومن ضل } عن الهدى، { فإنما يضل عليها } ، أي على نفسه، يقول: فعلى نفسه إثم ضلالته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No soul carries another soul's sin.
rows.anchor: يقول: لا تحمل نفس خطيئة نفس أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God did not punish anyone in worldly life until sending a messenger to warn that punishment was coming, as in 26:208.
rows.anchor: في الدنيا أحدا، { حتى نبعث رسولا } [آية: 15]، لينذرهم بالعذاب في الدنيا بأنه نازل بهم، كقوله سبحانه، { وما أهلكنا } في الدنيا { من قرية إلا لها منذرون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When God intends a town's worldly destruction, He multiplies its tyrants among its affluent people, who grow insolent, disobey, incur the decree already known by God, and are destroyed.
rows.anchor: { وإذآ أردنآ أن نهلك قرية } بالعذاب في الدنيا، { أمرنا مترفيها } ، يقوله: أكثرنا جبابرتها فبطروا في المعيشة، { ففسقوا فيها }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning to Mecca recalls how God destroyed many generations after Noah for their sins; no one knows His servants' sins better than God.
rows.anchor: يخوف كفار مكة بمثل عذاب الأمم الخالية، فقال سبحانه: { وكم أهلكنا } بالعذاب في الدنيا، { من القرون من بعد نوح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever wants immediate worldly life receives whatever wealth God wills for whomever He chooses, then is sent to Hell, blamed by God and driven away.
rows.anchor: { من كان يريد } في الدنيا، { العاجلة عجلنا له فيها } ، يعني في الدنيا، { ما نشآء لمن نريد } ، من المال، { ثم جعلنا له جهنم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage is said to have been revealed about three men from Thaqif, naming Farqad ibn Yamama, Abu Fatima ibn al-Bukhturi, and Safwan; the source then adds two unnamed placeholders.
rows.anchor: نزلت في ثلاثة نفر من ثقيف، فى: فرقد بن يمامة، وأبي فاطمة بن البحتري، وصفوان، وفلان، وفلان.
